context_summary: F104 Quick Win UX Polish — 8 visual/UX improvements identified from competitive TCG marketplace research. All are low-effort, high-impact frontend enhancements with no backend changes required. The project already has Recharts (for sparklines), a price history table (source_cards), currency service (for arbitrage), and a 100k+ card catalog (F103). These are purely additive UI improvements with no risk to existing functionality.

options_considered.description: Plan all 8 quick wins as a single feature with maximum Wave parallelization. Each improvement is independent, so most can run in parallel.
pros: All items are independent — no cross-dependencies between sparklines, hover previews, skeleton loading, etc.
Single feature keeps the scope contained and trackable
Maximizes parallelization — most tasks can run in the same Wave
All required data sources already exist (price history, currency rates, catalog)
Recharts is already in the project for sparklines
Low risk — purely additive frontend changes, no backend modifications
cons: 8 tasks in one feature is larger than typical, but all are small/focused
Merge conflicts possible if multiple tasks touch the same component — mitigated by Wave grouping

options_considered.description: Split into 2 features: F104 (price visualization) and F105 (UX polish).
cons: Unnecessary overhead — all items are quick wins, splitting doubles the ceremony
User explicitly asked for a single grouped feature
More merge coordination needed between two features

rationale: All 8 items are independent, low-risk, frontend-only quick wins. Grouping them in a single feature with parallel Waves minimizes overhead and matches the user's explicit request. The existing codebase already provides all required data and libraries. No backend changes needed.
